problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a real-valued convex function f on a real separable Hilbert space E. A global minimizer xstar exists with ||x0-xstar||≤R. Neither smoothness nor strong convexity is assumed.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MomentumLipschitzConvex.lean: Params; spec.admissible, ConvexOn and minimizer-existence clauses.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A query x returns grad(ξ,x). Independent samples ξ follow the hidden law M.law. The mean g(x)=Eξ[grad(ξ,x)] belongs to ∂f(x); individual replies need not themselves be subgradients. Only the vector reply is available.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MomentumLipschitzConvex.lean: Model; spec.Query, spec.Reply, and spec.admissible, infinitePi oracle law and mean-subgradient inequality.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform total second-moment bound Eξ||grad(ξ,x)||²≤G² for every x, including integrability. Consequently Eξ||grad(ξ,x)-g(x)||²≤G². Almost-sure boundedness and higher moments are not required.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MomentumLipschitzConvex.lean: spec.admissible, squared-norm integrability and second-moment bound.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is complete, real, and second-countable with its Borel measurable structure. G>0, R≥0, ε>0, x0, and β∈[0,1) are public; f, grad, and the sampling law are hidden. Permitted algorithms are restricted to constantMomentumSgd β γ N x0 for some γ and N. The initial-distance bound and mean-subgradient moment bound imply that f is G-Lipschitz.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MomentumLipschitzConvex.lean: Params; Model; spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.allowedAlgorithm, and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The E-valued output must have an integrable objective gap f(output)-f(xstar) for a global minimizer xstar, with its expectation at most ε. The successful predicate contains no separate averaging or iterate-selection requirement; the output is constrained through the permitted algorithm family.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E[f(output)-f(xstar)]≤ε under the product of the algorithm's randomness and the independent oracle-sample law. Oracle cost is bounded by the supplied deterministic budget for every seed realization.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MomentumLipschitzConvex.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence, product probability measure and per-seed call-count bound.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Convex stochastic subgradient optimization with independent samples, bounded second moments, a known initial-distance bound, and expected objective accuracy is a standard formulation. The permitted momentum family restricts the algorithms used to solve it.

descriptionHtml:
Momentum SGD for Convex Minimization

We consider minimizing a convex function f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. A given point x0∈E lies within distance R≥0 of a global minimizer x⋆. At x, the oracle returns g(ξ,x)∈E using a fresh independent sample ξ from a probability law ν on a measurable space Ξ. The map g is jointly measurable, its mean is a subgradient of f, and Eξ∼ν∥g(ξ,x)∥2≤G2, where G>0. For ε>0, constant-momentum SGD must return a last iterate x¯ with integrable objective gap satisfying E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε under the sampling law.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ξ, G, R, a momentum parameter β∈[0,1), ε, and x0; the objective, oracle map, and sampling law are accessed through oracle replies.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity). For every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y).

Assumption 2 (Stochastic subgradient oracle). The map g:Ξ×E→E is jointly measurable. For every x∈E, the random variable ∥g(ξ,x)∥2 is integrable under ν, and Eξ∼ν[∥g(ξ,x)∥2]≤G2. Writing h(x)=Eξ∼ν[g(ξ,x)] for the Bochner mean, we require f(x)+⟨h(x),y−x⟩≤f(y),x,y∈E. Successive calls use independent samples ξ0,ξ1,… with common law ν, and queries may be made anywhere in E.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze constant-momentum SGD with a linearly decreasing step-size schedule. The algorithm chooses γ∈R and N∈{0,1,2,…} from its inputs and initializes m0=0. At iteration k≥0, it queries the oracle at xk and updates gk=g(ξk,xk),mk+1=βmk+(1−β)gk,ηk=γ(N+1−k+β1−β),xk+1=xk−ηkmk+1. After T∈{0,1,2,…} oracle calls, the output is the last iterate x¯=xT. The schedule parameter N and the call budget T are separate quantities.

Let P=ν⊗N be the joint law of the samples. The required objective gap is integrable under P and satisfies EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• A. S. Nemirovskii and D. B. Yudin. Cesari Convergence of the Gradient Method of Approximating Saddle Points of Convex-Concave Functions. 1978. Complexity: O(1+G2R2/ε2) fixed stochastic subgradient calls for expected objective gap ≤ε, using averaged projected iterates on a radius-R ball.
  • Daniela Angela Parletta, Andrea Paudice, and Saverio Salzo. An Improved Analysis of the Clipped Stochastic subGradient Method under Heavy-Tailed Noise. 2024 preprint; version used: April 2025, v2. Complexity: O(1+G2R2/ε2) fixed stochastic subgradient calls for expected last-iterate objective gap ≤ε, with moment order p=2, batch size one, base stepsize R/G, and base clipping parameter G, for R>0.
  • Prateek Jain, Dheeraj Nagaraj, and Praneeth Netrapalli. Making the Last Iterate of SGD Information Theoretically Optimal. 2019, COLT; full analysis: May 2019 preprint, v2. Complexity: O(1+G2D2/ε2) fixed stochastic subgradient calls for expected last-iterate objective gap ≤ε, using projected SGD with epochwise decreasing stepsizes; D is the feasible-set diameter.

comparisonHtml:
Convex f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure; a minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. The jointly measurable oracle g(ξ,x) has ∫g(ξ,x)dp(ξ)∈∂f(x) and integrable squared norm with ∫∥g(ξ,x)∥2dp(ξ)≤G2 for every x. Samples are IID from the probability law p. Here G>0, R≥0, 0≤β<1, and ε>0. The setup restricts algorithms to constant-β EMA momentum SGD. Result (1) uses zero initial momentum and horizon-dependent affine step decay, tuned with G,R,β,ε, and returns xN with ∫[f(xN)−f(x⋆)]dP≤ε, where P=p⊗N.

Constant-momentum last-iterate guarantees for MomentumLipschitzConvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) ConstantMomentumLastIterate (Ours) (review) O(1+G2R2ε2+κ2log⁡e1−β)
(2) Linear-decay SGD (Liu and Zhou 2026, Thm. 3.4)

O(1+G2R2ε2)

Finite-dimensional Euclidean specialization: L=0, M=2G, σ≤G, no composite term or constraints.

 (1): Matches known accuracy dependence with log-free constant-EMA last-iterate analysis; no improved problem-class complexity. (1): Adds κ2loge1−β cost. Covers only unconstrained objectives; (2) also permits composite terms, constraints, and general norms.
(3) FTRL-SGDM (Li et al. 2022, Cor. 1)

O(1+G2R2ε2)

On Rd, second-moment assumption H3; c=R, anytime choice γt−1=R/(Gt).

 (1): Matches known accuracy dependence with constant EMA momentum instead of increasing momentum and shrinking updates; no total-cost improvement. (1): Needs the horizon; adds momentum-dependent cost and has a worse leading constant.
(4) Schedule-Free SGD (Defazio et al. 2024, Thm. 1)

O(1+G2R2ε2)

Special case on Rd: convex G-Lipschitz sample losses; constant interpolation parameter in [0,1]; horizon-tuned step.

 (1): Scope extends to second-moment-bounded oracles without Lipschitz sample losses. Returns the EMA last iterate; (4) certifies its averaged sequence, not its query sequence. (1): On the shared sample-loss setup, adds momentum-dependent cost and has a worse leading constant.

Abbr: κ=β/(1−β); N is the number of oracle calls; all costs count individual stochastic subgradient calls for expected objective gap ε. EMA: exponential moving average; FTRL: follow the regularized leader; SGD(M): stochastic gradient descent (with momentum). In (2), L,M are smoothness/Lipschitz parameters and σ bounds noise standard deviation; in (3), c,γt−1 are tuning parameters and t is the iteration index.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Sqrt
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic
import Mathlib.Probability.ProductMeasure

namespace OracleTemplate.MomentumConvex

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

noncomputable def stepSize (β γ : ℝ) (N k : ℕ) : ℝ := γ * ((N : ℝ) + 1 - k + β / (1 - β))

noncomputable def constantMomentumSgd (β γ : ℝ) (N : ℕ) (x0 : E) : Algorithm E E E where
  State := ℕ × E × E
  initial _ := (0, x0, 0)
  query s := (0, s.2.1)
  update s g :=
    (s.1 + 1, s.2.1 - stepSize β γ N s.1 • (β • s.2.2 + (1 - β) • g), β • s.2.2 + (1 - β) • g)
  output s := s.2.1

end OracleTemplate.MomentumConvex

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.MomentumLipschitzConvex

open OracleTemplate OracleTemplate.MomentumConvex

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ξ : Type
  [measurableΞ : MeasurableSpace Ξ]
  G : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  β : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE Params.measurableE Params.borelE
  Params.countableE Params.measurableΞ

structure Model (E Ξ : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Ξ] where
  law : ProbabilityMeasure Ξ
  f : E → ℝ
  grad : Ξ → E → E

noncomputable def scale (G R : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  R / (G * ((N : ℝ) + 2) * Real.sqrt ((N : ℝ) + 2))

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Model p.E p.Ξ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  allowedAlgorithm q algorithm :=
    ∃ (γ : ℝ) (N : ℕ), algorithm = constantMomentumSgd q.β γ N q.x0
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.G ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.β ∧ q.β < 1 ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q M O :=
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ξ
          law := ⟨Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => (M.law : Measure q.Ξ)), inferInstance⟩
          answer := fun _ (_, x) ξ => M.grad ξ x } ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry M.grad) ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ M.f ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ξ => ‖M.grad ξ x‖ ^ 2) (M.law : Measure q.Ξ)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ξ, ‖M.grad ξ x‖ ^ 2 ∂(M.law : Measure q.Ξ) ≤ q.G ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ x y, M.f x + inner ℝ (∫ ξ, M.grad ξ x ∂(M.law : Measure q.Ξ)) (y - x) ≤ M.f y) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn M.f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q M output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn M.f Set.univ xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => M.f (output ω) - M.f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, M.f (output ω) - M.f xstar ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.MomentumLipschitzConvex
